content.text: Governing law is New York; venue is New York courts; any arbitration is optional and seated in New York. This meets the preferred position, so no redline.

input.quote: Section 10.6 Submission to Jurisdiction. Each party submits to the nonexclusive jurisdiction of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York and of any New York State Court sitting in New York, New York for legal proceedings relating to this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 elects the internal laws of the State of New York (including GOL §§ 5-1401/5-1402) and even bars any amendment changing the governing law away from New York, which matches our preferred position. Section 10.6 submits the parties to the jurisdiction of the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York and the New York State courts sitting in New York, New York, with waiver of venue and forum non conveniens objections — the preferred New York County forum. The Article XI dispute resolution provisions do not displace the courts: mediation or binding arbitration is available only at the Requesting Party's election in respect of reacquisition requests (Section 11.2(a) expressly preserves the option to "institute a legal proceeding"), any such proceeding is held in New York, New York (Section 11.2(d)(i)), the neutrals must be experienced in New York law, and awards are enforceable in any court of competent jurisdiction. There is no mandatory arbitration and no foreign seat, so no walk-away risk. The only departure from the preferred wording is that the submission to jurisdiction is nonexclusive rather than exclusive; that is a minor sub-element (and preserves our own flexibility to sue elsewhere), so we note it rather than redline it.
